{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./sm_hsp_dimer_prod.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -t 24:00:00  -> -t 24h
#   -n 20        -> -n 20
#   -c 1         -> -c 1
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 20 -c 1 -t 24h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm -A youraccount not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: accounting/charging may not be applied as intended; site may require account/project out-of-band.

  # NOTE: Slurm -J SM_HSP_dimer_prod not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --error/--output used %j expansion (jobid) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  ml purge
  ml ABINIT/8.10.3 Armadillo/9.700.2 CDO/1.9.5 GOTM/5.3-221-gac7ec88d NCO/4.8.1 NCO/4.9.2 OpenFOAM/6 OpenFOAM/7 OpenFOAM/v1912 Rosetta/3.7 Siesta/4.1-MaX-1.0 Siesta/4.1-b4 Singular/4.1.2 XCrySDen/1.5.60 XCrySDen/1.6.2 deal.II/9.1.1-gcc deal.II/9.1.1-intel
  ml gromacs/2019.6.th

  # Preprocessing can run on 1 rank
  flux run -n 1 gmx grompp -f md.mdp -c npt.gro -t npt.cpt -p topol.top -o md_0_1.tpr

  # Run MD using 20 threads (kept from original)
  flux run -n 1 -c 20 gmx mdrun -nt 20 -deffnm md_0_1
fi
"
}

issues: This is a self-submitting pattern: it will only work if `flux batch` can connect to a Flux broker from where the script is executed (inside a Flux instance or via a site-provided submission endpoint).

Resource mismatch: the batch allocation requests 20 tasks (`-n 20 -c 1`), but the main step requests 1 task with 20 cores (`flux run -n 1 -c 20`). If Flux enforces that steps cannot exceed allocated cores-per-task, the step may be rejected or oversubscribe; even if it runs, most of the allocated task slots will be unused.
